claims.text: The homogenized Al0.7CoCrFeNi alloy initially has a dual-phase FCC/B2 lamellar structure.
The initial alloy is strong but brittle.
Brittleness arises from stress concentration and cracking at incoherent FCC/B2 interfaces.
The proposed intervention uses a hexahedron-anvil apparatus at 6 GPa and 1473 K for 2 hours.
HPHT treatment at 6 GPa and 1473 K for 2 hours will topologically transform the lamellar microstructure into a hierarchical pattern.
The HPHT-induced hierarchical structure will contain coherent FCC/B2 interfaces replacing incoherent lamellar boundaries.
Coherent interfaces facilitate dislocation transfer between phases.
Dislocation transfer across coherent interfaces alleviates interfacial stress concentrations.
The hierarchical coherent microstructure enables dislocation transfer, stacking faults, and twinning.
The activated deformation mechanisms produce a more homogeneous strain distribution and arrest interfacial cracking.
HPHT treatment will simultaneously enhance strength and ductility.
HPHT treatment will shift fracture morphology from isolated microcracks to elongated cracks.
The GND densities of the FCC and B2 phases will converge at high strain after HPHT treatment.
There is a pressure-temperature window that creates coherent interfaces without causing phase instability or decomposition.
A hexahedron-anvil apparatus provides uniform pressure application.
Conventional thermomechanical treatments cannot produce the same hierarchical coherence.
Failure of conventional cryo-rolling and annealing to produce hierarchical coherence or GND homogenization would falsify the HPHT hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The treatment input is described as homogenized, whereas the baseline is described as as-cast, so the stated baseline does not cleanly represent the untreated version of the specified initial state.

The boundary asserts that conventional treatments cannot achieve the same hierarchical coherence, but the falsification criterion says that observing this expected failure would falsify the HPHT hypothesis. Logically, successful reproduction by a conventional treatment—not failure—would challenge the claimed uniqueness of HPHT.
